question: In Economics, Total variable cost / Units of output produced = ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Average variable cost**__** .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Total Variable Cost (TVC) refers to costs that change with the level of output, such as **materials and labor.**
 
• Total Cost (TC) is calculated by adding fixed costs (which do not change with output) to total variable costs.
 
• Average Variable Cost (AVC) can be determined by dividing total variable costs by the number of units produced.
 
• Understanding TVC helps businesses optimize production levels and pricing strategies by analyzing cost behavior with changes in output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Cost (MC) **The change in total variable cost resulting from producing one additional unit can help determine the marginal cost of production, which is crucial for pricing decisions.
 
• Cost-Volume Relationship: Analyzing the relationship between total variable costs and output helps businesses understand how costs scale with production levels, assisting in budgeting and financial planning.
 
• Break-Even Analysis: Knowing total variable costs per unit aids in calculating the break-even point, where total revenue equals total costs, helping businesses assess profitability.
 
• Operational Efficiency: Monitoring total variable costs relative to output can highlight areas for improving operational efficiency, such as reducing waste or optimizing resource allocation.
